result.summary: Huang's 2018 AI forecasts that I could find were all about self-driving cars and came in the week of CES in January. The CES press Q&A gives robot taxis in 2019, level 3 around early 2020 and level 4 in late 2021, the same claim as the two recorded files dated 2018-05-10. reply_text:
I found two new 2018 predictions from Jensen Huang, both about self-driving cars and both from the week of CES in Las Vegas in January. I found nothing from him in 2018 about AGI or superintelligence, dated or not.

- **CES 2018 press Q&A (VentureBeat's edited transcript).** He said a level 3 car would ship "something along the lines of early 2020", a level 4 car "will probably be late 2021" and "a robot taxi, will probably be 2019." This is the same claim as your two files dated 2018-05-10. Those files carry a May date, though, and this is January. I've put both file names in `already_recorded`, but you may want to log January as a separate occasion or change the date.
- **Fortune Brainstorm Tech dinner, 8 January.** He said a car that drives itself everywhere in all conditions "won't be here for five to 10 years." This one is new. I only have it from Fortune's write-up of the evening, not a transcript.

**Left out:**
- At the GPU Technology Conference (GTC) in March he said "we're good for the next ten years." That was about how fast Nvidia's chips can keep improving, which is a chip forecast, not an AI one.
- In the CES Q&A he said flying taxis won't be a big part of "anybody's business in 10 years." That's a business forecast.
- An article on the May 2018 earnings call didn't include the robotaxi or 2020–21 dates. So I couldn't confirm where your May files come from, and I didn't open the call transcript.

**Not opened:** the full GTC, GTC Taiwan, GTC Europe and GTC China keynote videos. I used all 12 searches and 5 of the 6 page openings.
